name: Electromagnetic pulse damage to electronics
definition: Electronic equipment disabled by the electromagnetic pulse of a nuclear blast, and hardening against it.

first_pass.what: The Starfish Prime high-altitude nuclear test over the Pacific unexpectedly disrupted electronics in Hawaii, about 1,445 km away.

first_pass_note: Starfish Prime is the first observed large-scale damage. Earlier EMP effects (1945 onward) were not confirmed.

name: Speech recognition and voice command
definition: A machine that recognizes spoken words and carries out spoken commands, such as voice-operated doors or computers.

first_pass.what: Bell Labs' Audrey recognized the ten spoken digits from a single speaker.
Apple launched Siri, built into the iPhone 4S, putting voice command in ordinary users' hands.

first_pass_note: Voice-operated doors and locks were not researched.

name: Automatic dictation transcription
definition: A machine that listens to dictation and produces the written or typed text automatically.

first_pass.what: Dragon Systems released Dragon NaturallySpeaking 1.0, the first general-purpose continuous-speech dictation product for PCs. A discrete-speech DragonDictate (1990) is unverified.

first_pass_note: DragonDictate 1990 unverified. No demonstration milestone sourced.
doubt: 1997 NaturallySpeaking; earlier dictation products (DragonDictate 1990, IBM Tangora) may fit.

name: Speech synthesis
definition: A machine that generates spoken language with an artificial voice, such as a talking computer reading out answers.

first_pass.what: Bell Labs' Homer Dudley unveiled the keyboard-operated Voder speech synthesizer at the New York World's Fair.

first_pass_note: Voder was human-operated. The 1961 IBM Daisy Bell computer-synthesized speech is a later milestone.

name: Conversational natural-language computer
definition: A computer that holds a conversation in ordinary human language, understanding questions and replying in kind.

first_pass.what: Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT published ELIZA, a pattern-matching program that held typed conversations in English.

first_pass_note: ELIZA is a pattern-matching demonstration. Mass adoption (ChatGPT, 2022-23) was not sourced.

name: Machine translation
definition: A machine that automatically translates written or spoken language from one human language into another.

first_pass.what: The Georgetown-IBM experiment translated about 49-60 Russian sentences into English on an IBM computer.
The US Air Force's AN/GSQ-16 Automatic Language Translator was installed at Wright-Patterson's Foreign Technology Division for real translation work, and was later replaced by SYSTRAN in 1970.

name: Automatic decipherment of unknown languages
definition: A machine that learns or decodes a previously unknown language, such as an alien or lost tongue, from samples.
first_pass_note: No machine has decoded an unknown language from samples; no milestones given.

name: Codebreaking computer
definition: A machine that breaks enciphered messages by rapidly testing keys or analysing patterns in the ciphertext.

first_pass.what: Colossus Mark 1, built by Tommy Flowers's team, became operational at Bletchley Park against the Lorenz cipher. A working prototype existed by December 1943.

first_pass_note: Mark 1 operational 5 Feb 1944. Mark 2 ran 1 June 1944. Earlier electromechanical bombes were not considered.

name: Machine-generated writing
definition: A computer that composes stories, articles, poems or books automatically.

first_pass.what: Christopher Strachey's program on the Ferranti Mark 1 at Manchester generated love letters from templates and word lists.

first_pass_note: Only the earliest demonstration was sourced. Mass adoption (LLMs) not sourced.

name: Machine-composed music and art
definition: A computer or robot that composes or performs music, or produces pictures, without a human artist.

first_pass.what: Lejaren Hiller and Leonard Isaacson used the ILLIAC I at the University of Illinois to compose the Illiac Suite string quartet (sources say 1956 or 1957).

first_pass_note: AARON (Harold Cohen) search returned nothing. Only the earliest music milestone was sourced.

name: Machine learning
definition: A machine that improves its performance from experience or data instead of being explicitly programmed for each task.

first_pass.what: Arthur Samuel published a paper showing a checkers program that learned to play better than its programmer (IBM Journal of R&D).

first_pass_note: Rosenblatt's perceptron (1957-58) is an alternative early demonstration.

name: Computer chess
definition: A computer program that plays chess, eventually at or beyond the level of the best human players.

first_pass.what: Los Alamos's MANIAC I played a reduced 6x6 chess variant (Los Alamos chess). Deep Blue beat world champion Kasparov in May 1997, which reaches the 'best human level' clause but is not a listed kind.

first_pass_note: Turing's paper program (1951-52) was not sourced. Deep Blue is the 1997 superhuman milestone.

name: Game-playing computer (other games)
definition: A machine that plays games of skill or chance such as checkers, poker, bridge or Nim against people.

first_pass.what: Christopher Strachey's draughts program first ran on the Ferranti Mark 1 at Manchester in summer 1952, after an earlier failed run at NPL in 1951. Sources vary.

first_pass_note: Nimrod (1951) search returned nothing. Samuel's checkers program was televised on 1956-02-24.

name: Artificial general intelligence
definition: A machine that matches or exceeds human intelligence across essentially all intellectual tasks.

name: Sentient or self-aware machine
definition: A machine that has consciousness, self-awareness and an inner life of its own.
